summary: Fix keyboard-visible focus, make the checkout submit button reachable before the secondary shopping link, prevent the cart from flashing to an empty-cart state during slow order submission, and add non-visual accessible names/labels for controls that shoppers use in the purchase path.

edits.why: This restores a visible keyboard focus indicator on buttons such as Add To Cart and Place Order.
This lets the submit button come first in keyboard order while preserving the same visual button order for mouse users.
This makes tabbing after the final payment field land on Place Order instead of the secondary Continue Shopping control.
This restores a visible keyboard focus indicator on checkout text fields.
This turns visual checkout field labels into real programmatic labels.
This restores a visible keyboard focus indicator on checkout select fields.
This associates each checkout label with its corresponding input or select.

edits.find:
import { NextPage } from 'next';
import Head from 'next/head';
edits.why: This prepares the cart page to keep the checkout view stable while an order is being placed.
This tracks a pending order submission so slow devices are not shown an empty cart before navigation completes.
This prevents the empty-cart page from replacing checkout during a slow order submission.
This lets the cart page know when checkout submission has started.
This marks checkout as pending before the cart can be emptied and restores normal state only if submission fails.
This keeps the order submission callback up to date with the pending-state handler.

edits.find:
name="currency_code"
          onChange={(event: { target: { value: string; }; }) => setSelectedCurrency(event.target.value)}
edits.why: This gives the currency selector an accessible name without changing its visual design.
This gives the product quantity selector an accessible name for keyboard and assistive technology users.
This gives cart quantity selectors accessible names tied to their products.
This gives the header home link discernible text through the logo image alt text.
This marks the decorative banner image so it does not create an unlabeled image stop.
This identifies the page language for assistive technology.
